collection_state (src/sqllens/_memory_consistency.py:63-76) keys on (st_dev, st_ino, collection_name) from Path.stat(). Distinct directories have distinct inodes, so distinct state objects. Two spellings of one directory on a case-insensitive filesystem stat to the same dev/inode, so they return the identical object. The values are held in a WeakValueDictionary, but the left operand stays alive on the stack while the right is evaluated, so the `is` check in tests/unit/test_memory_listing_consistency.py:246 and 250 is sound.

The claim is universal, but the default testpaths (pyproject.toml:112: tests/unit, tests/integration) contain conditional skips: tests/unit/test_output_boundaries.py:47,108,125,150 skipif(NODE is None); tests/unit/test_preflight.py:127-229, test_safety_limits.py:388,399 and test_factory_wiring.py:481 use importorskip for psycopg2/pymysql; tests/unit/test_lockfile_guard.py:374 skipif(not LOCKFILE.exists()). collection_state (src/sqllens/_memory_consistency.py:63-76) keys its cache on (st_dev, st_ino, collection_name) from Path.stat(), not on the path string. On a case-sensitive filesystem, variant.mkdir() (test lines 243-250) creates a separate directory with a different inode, so the `is not` assertion depends on real identity keying. It would fail if the implementation collapsed distinct directories, for example by keying on collection name only. The first state stays referenced as a temporary during the comparison, so the WeakValueDictionary cannot recycle it. The same-directory branch (line 246) covers the sharing guarantee, so the pair is not vacuous.
